places.name: Gulbenkian Museum & Garden
places.note: Sixties modernism set in a wild garden of streams and stone paths. Ancient Egypt to Lalique inside. The garden alone is worth the trip.

places.name: MAAT
places.note: A low wave of white tiles on the Tejo, its roof a walkway you can climb. Next door, the old red-brick power station is part of the museum.

places.name: Pavilhão de Portugal
places.note: Siza's concrete canopy, hung like a sheet of paper between two porticoes. One of the great architectural gestures of the late 20th century. Stand beneath it.

places.name: Museu Nacional do Azulejo
places.note: Five centuries of tiles in a former convent, gilded chapel included. The long panorama of pre-earthquake Lisbon is the piece to find.

places.name: Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
places.note: The highest viewpoint in the old city, with the castle and the river in one look. Quieter than the famous lookouts; come at dusk.

places.name: Igreja de São Roque
places.note: A plain facade hiding one of the richest interiors in Europe. The chapel of St John the Baptist was built in Rome, then shipped to Lisbon in pieces.

places.name: Ler Devagar
places.address: LX Factory, Rua Rodrigues de Faria 103
places.note: A bookshop in an old printing works, shelves two storeys high and a bicycle flying overhead. Its name means 'read slowly'.

places.name: A Vida Portuguesa
places.note: Heritage Portuguese goods, from soaps and sardine tins to enamelware, in an old shop space. The best souvenirs in Lisbon, and none of them tacky.

places.name: Embaixada
places.note: A 19th-century neo-Moorish palace now full of Portuguese designers. Climb the main stair for the courtyard and the ceilings.

places.name: Taberna da Rua das Flores
places.note: A tiny tasca with the day's menu read aloud from a chalkboard. Petiscos, natural wine, no bookings. Join the queue before opening.

places.name: Cervejaria Ramiro
places.note: A loud seafood hall: carabineiros, clams in garlic, then a steak sandwich for dessert. A Lisbon institution. Go late.

places.name: Jerónimos Monastery
places.note: Manueline stone carved like rope and coral, built on spice money. The two-storey cloister is the heart of it.

places.name: Pastéis de Belém
places.note: The custard tart, from the original recipe since 1837. Skip the takeaway queue and walk through to the tiled rooms behind.

places.name: MAC/CCB
places.note: The contemporary art museum in Gregotti's stone cultural centre. The roof gardens look out over the river.

places.name: Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga
places.note: Portugal's old masters and the Nanban screens, in a palace above the docks. The garden café overlooks the river.

places.name: Casa-Museu Medeiros e Almeida
places.note: A collector's mansion of clocks, silver and porcelain, left just as he arranged it. Rarely busy.

places.name: Panteão Nacional
places.note: A white domed church that took nearly three centuries to finish. Climb to the terrace above the river.

places.name: Feira da Ladra
places.note: The 'thieves' market' flea market, Tuesdays and Saturdays, below the Pantheon. Tiles, records, old postcards.

places.name: Miradouro de Santa Catarina
places.note: A viewpoint over the bridge and the docks, where the neighbourhood gathers at sunset. A beer from the kiosk.

places.name: Jardim do Príncipe Real
places.note: A square garden built around one vast cedar, its branches trained into a shade canopy. A kiosk café and old men at cards.

places.name: Jardim Botânico de Lisboa
places.note: A terraced botanical garden of palms and cycads, falling down the hill behind the old Polytechnic. Shaded and calm.

places.name: Aqueduto das Águas Livres
places.note: An 18th-century aqueduct that survived the earthquake. Walk across its high arches above the Alcântara valley.

places.name: Mãe d'Água das Amoreiras
places.note: The aqueduct's reservoir: a still, stone cathedral of water. Climb to the roof for the view.

places.name: Fundação Arpad Szenes-Vieira da Silva
places.note: Vieira da Silva's labyrinth paintings in a former silk factory, beside the aqueduct. Small and absorbing.

places.name: Livraria Bertrand
places.note: Recorded as the oldest bookshop in the world still trading, in Chiado since 1732. Ask them to stamp your book.

places.name: A Brasileira
places.note: An Art Deco café of mirrors and dark wood, with Pessoa in bronze outside. A bica at the counter.

places.name: Gare do Oriente
places.note: Calatrava's station of white steel trees over the platforms. Arrive by metro and look up.

places.name: Museu do Oriente
places.note: Asian art and Portugal's links with the East, in a converted 1940s cod warehouse on the docks.

places.name: A Ginjinha
places.note: A hole-in-the-wall bar pouring sour-cherry liqueur since 1840. Ask for it 'com elas', with cherries.

places.name: Cinemateca Portuguesa
places.note: The national film archive, with repertory screenings and a terrace bar. Check the programme and go.

places.name: Convento do Carmo
places.note: A Gothic church left roofless by the 1755 earthquake. Its arches stand open to the sky.
